title: Some people think Joseph’s story is about a dream that came true.
paragraphs: Some people think Joseph’s story is about a dream that came true.
But it is really about a dream that survived suffering.

Joseph received the dream as a teenager.
But the fulfillment did not come for many years.
In between the dream and the palace were seasons that looked like complete failure.

He was betrayed by his brothers.
Sold as a slave.
Falsely accused.
Thrown into prison.
And forgotten by someone he helped.
Imagine the questions Joseph could have asked God.

“Why show me the dream if this is my reality?”
“Why give me a vision of leadership while I sit in a prison cell?”
But Joseph’s story reveals something many of us misunderstand.
God often reveals the destination long before we are ready to carry it.
Because the process is what prepares the person.
Joseph learned administration in Potiphar’s house.
He learned resilience in betrayal.
He learned integrity when no one was watching.
He learned patience in prison.
And he learned to trust God when life made no sense.
By the time Pharaoh needed a man to manage the greatest economic crisis of the ancient world, Joseph was no longer just a dreamer.
He was a man shaped by hardship, humility, and faith.
And when Joseph finally stood before Pharaoh, the palace was not creating him.
It was simply revealing what the hidden years had already built.
Here is the quiet truth Joseph’s story teaches us:
A dream from God does not eliminate the process of God.
Sometimes the longest seasons are the most important ones.
Because God is not only preparing the blessing.
He is preparing you.
And when the time finally comes, the world will see the promotion.
But only heaven will know the years that prepared it.
Have you ever experienced a season where it felt like your life was moving backward instead of forward?
